How to distinguish order refunds, parcel refunds, original returns and balance movements before contacting support.

LoloBuy refund status: how to read bills before contacting support

A LoloBuy refund status is easiest to understand when you begin with the exact transaction, not the amount you expected to receive. The account can record several different money movements: an order payment, an order refund, a parcel payment, a parcel refund, an original return, a balance recharge or a balance withdrawal. Two records may show the same amount while representing different stages or destinations.

The current LoloBuy bill interface uses statuses including Pending payment, Paid, Pending refund, Completed, Cancelled and Error. It also labels refund subjects such as Order refund, Parcel refund and Original return. These labels are useful evidence, but none should be interpreted in isolation as a promise about when money will appear in a bank, card, wallet or account balance.

1. Identify the transaction before interpreting the status

Open the Bill page and find the record by its transaction number, business number, subject, time and amount. Do not search only by amount. A purchase and its later refund can appear as separate entries, and a shipping adjustment can be unrelated to a product-order refund even when both involve the same account.

Write down five fields privately: transaction type, transaction number, linked business number, displayed status and currency or amount. If the entry expands to show channel information, business information or a payment record, preserve those details as well. This creates a clear chain between the original payment and the refund entry.

Keep order numbers, parcel numbers and bill numbers separate. An order number identifies the product purchase. A parcel number identifies the international shipment. A transaction or bill number identifies the money movement. Support needs the reference that matches the refund type, not a random identifier copied from the same account.

2. Read each bill status literally

Pending payment means the bill has not reached the paid state shown in the account. It is not evidence that a bank declined the transaction, and it is not a refund status. Before retrying, check whether another bill or bank authorization already exists for the same business number.

Paid records a completed payment state. It does not mean the order has been purchased, stored, shipped or refunded. Those outcomes belong to the linked order or parcel workflow. Use the payment entry to prove that money was recorded, then check the business record for what happened next.

Pending refund indicates that the refund has not yet reached the bill’s completed state. Do not report it as money already returned. Completed is the bill status used for a finished refund record, but the receiving destination still matters. Check whether the transaction subject and channel point to account balance, the original payment route or another supported destination.

Cancelled means that bill will not continue as an active payment or refund record. Error signals that the record needs investigation; it does not explain the cause. In either case, preserve the transaction number and related business record before asking support what action is appropriate.

3. Separate an order refund from a parcel refund

An Order refund concerns the product-order side of the workflow. It may follow a canceled purchase, seller issue, return or another order-level resolution. The order page may separately show statuses such as returning or returned, and the return or exchange form asks for an application type and reason. Those operational labels should be checked alongside the bill.

A Parcel refund concerns the international parcel side. It can relate to the shipment transaction rather than the seller’s product payment. LoloBuy’s current parcel-payment notice says a difference between estimated and actual shipping cost can lead to an additional payment or refund communicated through an in-site message. That does not make every parcel refund a freight adjustment, so use the linked parcel and message to identify the reason.

Do not combine the two in one vague request. “My refund is missing” gives support little to verify. “The bill subject is Parcel refund, linked to parcel [private number], and the bill status is Pending refund” identifies the correct workflow without assuming why the record was created.

4. Treat “Original return” as a transaction subject, not an arrival guarantee

The Bill page can label a transaction as Original return. That label distinguishes the route from other account movements, but it does not by itself prove that the receiving bank, card or payment provider has posted the money. The LoloBuy record and the external payment statement are two different pieces of evidence.

Confirm the original payment method and compare the transaction reference, currency and amount. Check the account holder’s statement rather than another card or wallet. Some institutions display reversals, released authorizations and posted credits differently, so describe exactly what appears instead of calling every change a refund.

If LoloBuy shows Completed but the receiving statement has no matching credit, save both records with dates and masked identifiers. Ask which refund reference or channel number can be used to trace the transaction. Do not publish full card numbers, bank details, payment tokens or screenshots containing an unmasked address.

5. Do not confuse account balance with money returned outside LoloBuy

The Bill area has an Account balance and a balance-detail history. A refund or manual adjustment may affect the platform balance, while an original-channel return concerns an external payment destination. A larger balance is not automatically proof that a card refund occurred, and a completed external refund does not necessarily create spendable platform balance.

Use the balance history to look for the transaction type, income or expenditure amount, time, transaction number and resulting account balance. Compare the sequence rather than the final total alone. Purchases, recharges, refunds and deductions can all change the total between two checks.

Balance withdrawal is another separate action. Availability, destination, fees, limits and processing rules are displayed in the live withdrawal interface and may depend on the channel. Do not begin a withdrawal simply to test whether a refund exists. First establish whether the refund was intended for balance or the original payment route.

6. Reconcile the amount without inventing the cause of a difference

Compare the original business amount, discount, payment-channel information and refund amount shown in the bill details. An order can contain product price, domestic freight, discounts or later adjustments; a parcel can contain estimated and final shipping figures. A difference is a question to document, not evidence of an improper deduction.

Keep the displayed currency attached to every number. If the payment was shown in one currency and an external statement uses another, do not compare the raw digits as though they were the same denomination. Exchange rates and payment-channel fees can affect an external statement, but the article cannot determine which factor applies to an individual transaction.

Ask support to explain the calculation using the business number and bill details. A useful request identifies the original paid amount, refund amount, currency, transaction subject and the specific difference. Avoid demanding a fixed outcome based on a screenshot from another buyer or an old exchange rate.

7. Prevent a duplicate action while the record is unclear

If a payment screen times out or returns to an uncertain state, do not immediately pay again. Check the Bill page, linked order or parcel and external payment authorization first. A second attempt can create another bill or authorization that complicates the refund trail.

Likewise, do not submit repeated return, cancellation or refund requests for the same item unless support instructs you to do so. Keep one evidence chain: the original order or parcel, the application or message, the refund bill and any external statement. Repeated actions with different descriptions make it harder to identify the active case.

A bank dispute or chargeback is not a substitute for understanding the account record. It can introduce a separate process with its own evidence and consequences. If the LoloBuy bill is pending or unclear, first request a written explanation and preserve the response before deciding what formal remedy is appropriate.

8. Build a refund-status support packet

Prepare the transaction subject, transaction number, business number, displayed status, amount and currency, original payment method, date of the most recent status change and the exact question. Add the related order or parcel number only when it matches the bill. Attach a full account screenshot and a masked external statement when relevant.

Use direct wording: “Bill [private number] is labeled Order refund and currently shows Pending refund. It links to order [private number]. The original payment method was [method]. Please confirm the current refund route and whether you need any action or evidence from me.”

Send the packet through the private, transaction-aware support channel and keep replies in one conversation. Check in-site messages because LoloBuy uses them for payment and parcel adjustments. Never post private references in a public review, and never send a password, verification code or complete card data to someone claiming they can accelerate a refund.

Final LoloBuy refund-status checklist

Find the exact bill and classify it as an order refund, parcel refund, original return, balance movement or withdrawal. Match its transaction number to the correct business number. Read Pending refund and Completed literally. Then confirm the intended destination, amount, currency and external statement without mixing platform balance with bank or card activity.

If anything remains unclear, pause duplicate payments or applications and send one evidence-based request. LoloBuy’s bill labels can show where a refund sits in the platform workflow; the receiving statement shows whether the destination has recorded it. Keeping those two records separate is the safest way to investigate a LoloBuy refund status without inventing a timeline or outcome.
